verdict: The accepted version keeps every headline claim, the abstract and the parent-state framing, but adds a set of targeted controls that look referee-driven: Feenstra-normalised maps against set-point effects, T-matrix simulations and topography against defect-induced anisotropy, a Cs-terminated surface and a new x = 0.04 doping, error bars on the dispersions, and a caveat that the kz = pi DFT cut is only a qualitative reference. The text also now confronts the 'is this just nematic?' question, explains the residual QPI in CDW samples by orbital origin, adds an ARPES mass-renormalisation comparison, and hedges T* with a note that resistance shows no anomaly and that T* awaits temperature-dependent probes. The most demanding concerns of the old review, scanner and drift systematics, extrinsic strain, a measured T*, and gap-level evidence for a chiral-nematic superconductor, are not answered with new data and were likely rebutted in the response letter. These inferences come from the changes alone and may be wrong.

inferred_requests.title: Rule out defect scattering as the source of the anisotropy
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked whether oriented or strong-scattering defects (including Ti substituents) could produce the direction-dependent QPI, and asked for defect identification and simulation.

inferred_requests.title: Exclude the set-point effect
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked whether the set-point effect in constant-current dI/dV maps could distort the q positions, and asked for normalised maps.

inferred_requests.title: Give uncertainties and the fit window for the velocities
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked for error bars on q(E) and the velocities, the fitting range relative to the kink, and whether direction differences exceed the q resolution.

inferred_requests.title: Justify the kz = pi DFT comparison
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely questioned comparing QPI with a single kz = pi DFT cut and asked how quantitative the comparison is.

inferred_requests.title: Show the state is more than ordinary nematicity
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely argued the QPI looks C2-nematic, like known CDW-phase nematicity, and asked what distinguishes chiral-nematic from nematic and from the chiral CDW.

inferred_requests.title: Rule out a surface effect
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked whether the symmetry breaking is set by the Sb surface or tip-cleaned area rather than the bulk, and asked for another termination.

inferred_requests.title: Show reproducibility across samples and dopings
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked for more samples and dopings and a clear summary of where chiral QPI is seen.

inferred_requests.title: Support or temper the T* estimate
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely objected that T* is estimated from a low-temperature energy splitting, not measured, and asked for temperature dependence or bulk evidence.

inferred_requests.title: Link the residual QPI in CDW samples to the parent state
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked why the anisotropic QPI at x = 0.05 is not simply caused by the stripe or CDW order, and how it relates to the x = 0.15 features.

inferred_requests.title: Make the model and mechanism explicit
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked for a consistent definition of the distortion and phase, and an explicit description of the proposed sublattice charge order, including whether a lattice channel is possible.

inferred_requests.title: Reconcile mass renormalisation with ARPES
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely pointed out that the QPI mass enhancements differ from ARPES electron-phonon results and asked for an explanation.

inferred_requests.title: Clarify the superconducting-state evidence and the phase diagram
inferred_requests.text: A referee possibly questioned the B-QPI evidence for a chiral-nematic superconductor and asked how the gap types fit the phase diagram.

inferred_requests.title: Provide supplementary data and raw data
inferred_requests.text: The missing supplementary material and a data availability statement were supplied; this may be a journal requirement rather than a referee request.

inferred_requests.title: Fix citations
inferred_requests.text: A referee possibly flagged the duplicate reference and the roton preprint cited for the crystal structure.

issue_status.reason: Error bars now include pixel resolution and the text appeals to high q resolution, but no rotated-scan, tip-change, raw-Bragg or Lawler-Fujita controls appear in the main text.
No strain analysis; the text only concedes the pattern looks nematic and that a lattice channel could in principle generate the state.
T* is still not measured and stays in the title and phase diagram, but caveats on resistance and future temperature-dependent probes were added.
An orbital-origin argument for the residual QPI was added, but the 'descend from' claim, single-bias CDW ratios and handedness locking are unchanged.
One sign convention is now used and the sublattice model is written out in Methods, but phi is still chosen rather than fitted and the velocity anisotropy and Landau pinning are not addressed.
Error bars and a low-energy fit window were added and values re-extracted, but no velocity uncertainties, window sensitivity or correction to v_F = 2v_s are given.
No new analysis of short-range CDW correlations at x = 0.15 is visible in the main text.
Chiral QPI on the Cs-terminated surface is reported, but bulk probes of the doped samples and tip-cleaning effects are not discussed.
Dispersions re-extracted from Feenstra-normalised L(r,E) maps with a new Methods section.
Ti dopants identified, topography (Supplementary Fig. 13) said to show no dominant oriented defect population, and T-matrix simulations argue defects do not reproduce the geometry.
A new doping, a new termination and a Fig. 4g summary were added, but no tabulated counts of samples, fields of view or handedness.
Supplementary Figs. 1-20 and a public raw-data deposit are now provided.
An extra supplementary figure is cited but the 'chiral-nematic SC ground state' claim and its reasoning are unchanged.
The C6 wording is clarified and the state is distinguished from the chiral CDW, but no point-group classification is given and 'chiral' is kept.
The kz = pi cut is justified and called qualitative, but SOC, VCA, cutoff and k-mesh are unchanged.
The 3% RbV3Sb5 comparison is kept unchanged.
Fig. 4f caption unchanged; a separate data summary (Fig. 4g) was added but the conjectural regions are not marked.
'Discovery', 'direct evidence', 'unprecedented' and 'demonstrating ... descend from' remain.
No text change; panel order cannot be confirmed from the text layer.
Fig. 4b caption still says 1a0 x 4a0 while the text says 4a0 x 1a0.
Fig. 2c caption still says profiles are 'in (a)' and refers to dotted curves.
3D perspective renderings kept as the main evidence panels.
The Gauss-like background subtraction was replaced by masking the low-frequency centre.
'fall within the range of 1.29–1.71' kept although alpha-band 1.19 is below it.
Six-figure precision kept; no eV·Å units.
No energy resolution or step sizes added to the main text.
Fig. 3a was rebuilt from normalised maps with a new background treatment, so the old banding critique may no longer apply.
Colours for q vectors were added to Fig. 1g, but the green out-of-plane contours are still unlabeled in Fig. 1c.
Duplicate reference removed and roton preprint dropped for the crystal structure, but the UTe2 paper is still cited for the affine correction.

unaddressed_major.title: Scanner, drift and tip systematics
unaddressed_major.why: The new appeal to 'high q-space resolution' and pixel-resolution error bars suggests a referee raised resolution, and the authors argued rather than adding rotated-scan or tip-change controls.

unaddressed_major.title: Indistinguishable from nematic or strain
unaddressed_major.why: The new 'at first glance ... strongly nematic' passage and the 'lattice and electronic channels' hedge read like answers to a nematic/strain objection, with no strain analysis added.

unaddressed_major.title: T* not measured
unaddressed_major.why: Caveats about resistance and future nano-ARPES suggest the point was raised and answered by argument while the title and phase diagram stayed.

unaddressed_major.title: B-QPI does not show a chiral-nematic gap
unaddressed_major.why: A new supplementary B-QPI figure was added but the claim was kept verbatim, suggesting a defence rather than a concession.

unaddressed_major.title: Short-range CDW at x = 0.15
unaddressed_major.why: No trace of the concern in the main text; the new orbital-origin and defect discussions do not touch it.
